glosses: to sign (to give legal consent by writing one's signature)

examples.text: Er unterzeichnet den Brief eines Beamten.
examples.translation: Il signe la lettre d'un fonctionnaire.

examples.text: Die Zusammenarbeit zwischen den Hafenbehörden von Rotterdam und Basel soll daher weiter vertieft werden. Dazu wurde im Beisein von Bundesrätin Sommaruga auf einer Hafenrundfahrt eine Absichtserklärung unterzeichnet.
examples.translation: La coopération entre les autorités portuaires de Rotterdam et de Bâle doit donc encore être approfondie. Une déclaration d’intention a été signée à cet effet en présence de la conseillère fédérale Simonetta Sommaruga pendant une croisière dans le port.

examples.text: Der Staatschef hat nun acht Tage Zeit, um das Gesetz zu unterzeichnen. Dieses Mal kann der praktizierende Katholik Rebelo de Sousa das Inkrafttreten des Paragraphenwerks nicht aufhalten.
examples.translation: Le chef de l'État dispose désormais de huit jours pour signer la loi. Cette fois-ci, le catholique pratiquant Rebelo de Sousa ne pourra pas empêcher l’entrée en vigueur de la loi.

examples.text: Bundespräsident Frank-Walter Steinmeier hatte das umstrittene Gesetz nach längerer Prüfung und entgegen mehrerer Bitten vonseiten der DUH am Montag unterzeichnet.

glosses: eine Unterschrift geben, zum Beispiel als Zustimmung zu einem Vertrag

examples.text: Sie müssen nur noch hier unten unterzeichnen.

„Die Bauern sind beinahe alle Analphabeten, das sind aber auch viele der großen Fürsten, die sich metallene Petschaften mit ihrer Unterschrift gravieren lassen, sodass sie Dokumente nicht unterzeichnen müssen, sondern nur zu stempeln brauchen und damit verhehlen könnnen, dass sie unfähig sind, ihren eigenen erlauchten Namen zu schreiben.“
„Gouverneur Dannel P. Malloy hat ein entsprechendes Gesetz unterzeichnet. Connecticut erkennt damit Weißkopf als ersten Motorflieger der Geschichte an.“

glosses: A visible fact that shows that something exists or may happen.

examples.text: Their angry expressions were a clear sign they didn't want to talk.
Those clouds show signs of raining soon.
Those clouds show little sign of raining soon.

Although the Celebrity was almost impervious to sarcasm, he was now beginning to exhibit visible signs of uneasiness, the consciousness dawning upon him that his eccentricity was not receiving the ovation it merited.
No, I don't know why you're not fair / I give you my love, but you don't care / So what is right and what is wrong? / Gimme a sign

glosses: A visible fact that shows that something exists or may happen.

examples.text: "It's a sign of the end of the world," the doom prophet said.

glosses: A visible fact that shows that something exists or may happen.
A property of the body that indicates a disease and, unlike a symptom, can be detected objectively by someone other than the patient.

examples.text: Signs of disease are objective, whereas symptoms are subjective.

glosses: A mark or another symbol used to represent something.

examples.text: The sharp sign indicates that the pitch of the note is raised a half step.
I gave them a thumbs-up sign.

The sound of the Orlando dinner train whistle reminds me that it ' s already Friday, an auditory sign. Another auditory sign, a distant thunder clap, warns me of limited computer time before our evening thunderstorm moves in.

glosses: Physical evidence left by an animal.

examples.text: The hunters found deer sign at the end of the trail.

Animal sign is the key to eliminating guesswork when setting your traps. Only trap where there is sign. Sign is anything the animal leaves as a trace that indicates it may have passed through the area.

glosses: A clearly visible object, generally flat, bearing a short message in words or pictures.

examples.text: The sign in the window advertised a room for rent.
I missed the sign at the corner so I took the wrong turn.
The shops were, therefore, distinguished by painted signs, which gave a gay and grotesque aspect to the streets.
And thou shalt take this rod in thine hand, wherewith thou shalt do signs.
Your sign is Taurus? That's no surprise.

glosses: Positive or negative polarity, as denoted by the + or - sign.

examples.text: I got the magnitude right, but the sign was wrong.

glosses: A specific gesture or motion used to communicate by those with speaking or hearing difficulties; now specifically, a linguistic unit in sign language equivalent to word in spoken languages.

examples.text: And why not, as well as our dumbe men dispute, argue and tell histories by signes?

In American Sign Language (ASL), for instance, the sign for 'catch' is formed with one hand (in the role of agent) moving across the body (an action) to grasp the forefinger of the other hand (the patient).
Sorry, I don't know sign very well.

glosses: A semantic unit, something that conveys meaning or information (e.g. a word of written language); (linguistics, semiotics) a unit consisting of a signifier and a signified concept. (See sign (semiotics).)

examples.text: A Noun substantive and a Noun adjective may be thus distinguished, that a substantive may have the sign a or the before it; as, puer, a boy, the boy; but an adjective cannot, as, bonus, good.
A Pronoun is a Noun implying a Person, but not admitting the Sign a or the before it.
And some linguistic signs, like “the”, “and” or “with”, may lack apparent objects, though they are clearly meaningful and interpretable.

glosses: A military emblem carried on a banner or standard.

examples.text: The great Ensign of Messiah blaz'd Aloft by Angels born, his Sign in Heav'n.

glosses: To seal (a document etc.) with an identifying seal or symbol.

examples.text: The Queen signed her letter with the regal signet.

glosses: To mark, to put or leave a mark on.

examples.text: Meantime revolving in his thoughtful mind / The scar, with which his manly knee was sign'd […].

glosses: To validate or ratify (a document) by writing one's signature on it.

examples.text: Enquire the Iewes house out, giue him this deed, / And let him signe it […].

glosses: More generally, to write one's signature on (something) as a means of identification etc.

examples.text: I forgot to sign that letter to my aunt.

glosses: To write (one's name) as a signature.

examples.text: Just sign your name at the bottom there.
I received a letter from some woman who signs herself ‘Mrs Trellis’.
Please sign on the dotted line.

glosses: To finalise a contractual agreement to work for a given sports team, record label etc.

examples.text: Agents say Wales back Gavin Henson has signed for Cardiff Blues.

glosses: To engage (a sports player, musician etc.) in a contract.

examples.text: It was a great month. I managed to sign three major players.

glosses: To make the sign of the cross
To bless (someone or something) with the sign of the cross; to mark with the sign of the cross.

examples.text: We receive this child into the congregation of Christ's flock, and do sign him with the sign of the cross.
At the baptismal ceremony the child was […] signed with the cross in holy water.

glosses: To make the sign of the cross

examples.text: Shaking a fist at him with one fierce arm, / Signing himself with the other because of Christ.

glosses: To communicate using a gesture or signal.

examples.text: I signed to Brown to make his retreat.

glosses: To communicate or make known (a meaning, intention, etc.) by a sign.

examples.text: Pierre signed his acquiescence, and Isabel proceeded:
He signed me that I should follow him through the doorway.

glosses: To furnish (a road etc.) with signs.
To calculate or derive whether a quantity has a positive or negative sign.

examples.text: Un gardien dont le rôle était de donner aux croque-morts décharge, sur un registre, des cercueils qu'il avait comptés et vu inhumer, signa le livre et apposa son timbre en marge.
Remarquez bien, mes enfants déclare le grand-père, qui ne sait ni A ni B, signe à peine son nom, mais calcule de tête comme un notaire, tout le mal monte de la Vallée, et toujours.

glosses: Avaliser, endosser un acte en y apposant une signature.

examples.text: […]: de grands embarras financiers avaient conduit le gouvernement à signer avec des compagnies de chemin de fer des conventions que les radicaux avaient dénoncées comme étant des actes de brigandage ; […].

glosses: Action de signer, de marquer un mot ou une partie du texte dans un wiki ou un document électronique par cliquer ou cliquer et tirer.

examples.text: Il faut signer le mot avant couper ou copier-coller.
Avant elle, dans les sphaignaies encore flottantes, se trouve O. sphagnicola, à chapeau plus pâle et écailleux, qui signe au contraire un dynamisme de la sphaignaie.
Martin a signé avec ce club de football.
J’ai signé pour deux ans, pour une saison.
Les réseaux d'initiative publique peinent toujours à se commercialiser, même si de plus en plus de fournisseurs d'accès Internet (FAI) nationaux signent avec les opérateurs de ces RIP.

glosses: Revendiquer un acte, y laisser une empreinte singulière volontairement reconnaissable.

examples.text: Cette manœuvre est signée, on en devine facilement l’auteur.
Je persiste et signe.
Mais l’interdiction de signer dans les classes perdurera [en France] jusque dans les années 1970.
Une interprète a signé l’ensemble du discours du directeur.

glosses: Engager, recruter en parlant d’un sportif ou d’un artiste.

examples.text: Personne ne veut le signer en France.
Complètement épuisé, j'ai commencé à mal jouer. Et là, j’ai découvert un truc intéressant. Quand son adversaire jouait mal, Kučera prenait le pli, signant lui aussi une piètre performance.
En France, la période révolutionnaire signe la disparition de l’Académie royale des sciences.
